title: Truth (Shabbat 55a)
hookLine: the seal of the Holy One is truth
last: NOTHING BETTER THAN SILENCE, SAID THE SAGE.

cards: A letter closed with wax carries a little picture pressed into it. If the wax is broken, someone opened the letter. If the picture is a bad copy, the forger is caught.
A seal says: this really came from me, and nothing changed on the way. Kings had seals. Merchants had them.
And the Talmud says God has one too. In tractate Shabbat, a rabbi named Chanina names the picture on that seal, and he needs only one word to do it.

teach.h: THE SEAL OF THE HOLY ONE IS TRUTH.
teach.b: Emet. Truth. You met it early on, as one of the three things the world stands on.
Rabbi Chanina's saying is short: the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth. Turn it four ways.

teach.h: ALEF, MEM, TAV: FIRST TO LAST.
teach.b: First, the seal. A seal is pressed, not painted: what shows in the wax is exactly what was carved on the ring.
Calling truth God's seal says that what comes from God matches what is really there, with no gap between the face and the mark. Second, the letters. Emet is spelled alef, mem, tav.
Alef opens the Hebrew alphabet and tav closes it, with mem in between.

Elsewhere in the same tractate, the Talmud notices that the letters of truth stand far apart, and some teachers read a picture in it: truth runs from beginning to end, and holds at every point along the way.
The prophet Zechariah tells the people to speak truth, each one with a neighbor. Speak truly, and you press a small copy of that seal into an ordinary day.
Mussar teachers list truth among the traits to work on, like patience: one honest sentence at a time.
Fourth, truth with a heart. In tractate Ketubot, the Talmud records an argument about what to sing while dancing before a bride. The school of Shammai says: describe her as she is.
The school of Hillel says: sing, a beautiful and graceful bride. The discussion asks how truth and kindness live together.
Truth, here, is a seal, not a weapon. And it sits close to yesterday's silence: say less, and let what you say be true.

how: Mussar groups often take truthfulness as a trait to work on for a stretch of weeks, noting each day where they shaded the truth and where they spoke it, and studying sayings like Rabbi Chanina's together.

o: faith, believing what you cannot see
an oath, sworn to make a promise binding
truth, which the Talmud calls God's seal

p: the seal of the Holy One is truth

s: the saying about God's seal comes from the Torah itself
it comes from the Talmud, tractate Shabbat 55a, in the name of Rabbi Chanina.
the word emet runs from the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet to the last
alef opens the alphabet and tav closes it, with mem in between.
in the bride debate, the Talmud shows no concern for kindness
the schools of Shammai and Hillel argue over how truth and kindness live together.

games.q: you're dancing before a bride at her wedding. what do you sing about her?
o: describe her exactly as she is.
sing: a beautiful and graceful bride.
games.why: both answers are in the Talmud: Shammai's school says describe her as she is, Hillel's school says a beautiful and graceful bride. the debate is about truth and kindness together.

practice: Let one truth you've been avoiding come to mind: a yes you meant as a no, a thank-you never said, a mistake you let someone else carry.

Shape it into one plain sentence a friend could hear without flinching, true and kind at once, the way Hillel's school would want it. If you pray, bring that sentence into prayer; if not, just hold it steady.

wordCard.voice: Emet. Truth: alef, mem, tav, from the first letter to the last. The Talmud calls it the seal of the Holy One. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the seal is truth. One true sentence is a small copy of the seal. See you tomorrow.
